claims.old: ## 1. Introduction
claims.new: ## 1. Introduction

claims.old: Purpose.
claims.new: #### Purpose

claims.old: Redstone is a framework for modeling and simulating hierarchical hybrid causal systems (models that mix continuous dynamics, periodic discrete dynamics and events, exchanging values through directed ports).
claims.new: Redstone is a framework for modeling and simulating hierarchical hybrid causal systems (models that mix continuous dynamics, periodic discrete dynamics and events, exchanging values through directed ports).

claims.old: Its home domain is aircraft guidance, navigation and control: vehicle dynamics, sensors and avionics, simulated offline or interactively in real time.
claims.new: Its home domain is aircraft guidance, navigation and control: vehicle dynamics, sensors and avionics, simulated offline or interactively in real time.

claims.old: The formalism itself is domain-neutral.
claims.new: The formalism itself is domain-neutral.

claims.old: Capabilities.
claims.new: #### Capabilities

claims.old: A model is written as a tree of components in plain Julia.
claims.new: An author writes a tree of components (the units of modeling) in plain Julia.

claims.old: The build checks the tree.
claims.new: The build checks the tree.

claims.old: A simulation runs a `Model` (the tree compiled at one scalar type, ready to step) (§9).
claims.new: A simulation runs a `Model` (the tree compiled at one scalar type, ready to step) (§9).

claims.old: The framework provides these capabilities.
claims.new: The framework provides these capabilities.

claims.old: Continuous dynamics with algebraic outputs, integrated on a fixed step, with events either located by root-finding or checked at step boundaries (§2, §10).
claims.new: Continuous dynamics with algebraic outputs, integrated on a fixed step, with events either located by root-finding or checked at step boundaries (§2, §10).

claims.old: Multi-rate periodic discrete dynamics at declared sample times, held zero-order between ticks (§3.2, §10.5).
claims.new: Multi-rate periodic discrete dynamics at declared sample times, held zero-order between ticks (§3.2, §10.5).

claims.old: A build that derives the execution order from declared feedthrough and rejects algebraic loops by naming the cycle (§5, §9).
claims.new: A build that derives the execution order from declared feedthrough and rejects algebraic loops by naming the cycle (§5, §9).

claims.old: A runtime periphery (the devices, GUI and scripts that exchange data with a running simulation) that writes by staging and reads by snapshot (§11, §12).
claims.new: A runtime periphery (the devices, GUI and scripts that exchange data with a running simulation) that writes by staging and reads by snapshot (§11, §12).

claims.old: An input trace that replays any run bit-identically (§11.5).
claims.new: An input trace that replays any run bit-identically (§11.5).

claims.old: Stopped-sim services for initialization, trim and linearization, with exact automatic-differentiation Jacobians (§14).
claims.new: Stopped-sim services for initialization, trim and linearization, with exact automatic-differentiation Jacobians (§14).

claims.old: Design criteria.
claims.new: #### Design criteria

claims.old: The design answers to five criteria.
claims.new: The design answers to five criteria.

claims.old: Wherever it admits a capability it does not build, that capability is weighed against them as a guarded addition.
claims.new: It weighs each guarded addition (a capability it admits but does not build) against them.

claims.old: Zero-allocation stepping and type stability.
claims.new: Zero-allocation stepping and type stability.

claims.old: The inner loop allocates nothing, and the test suite asserts it (§7.5, §9.7).
claims.new: The continuous hot path allocates nothing, and CI asserts it (§7.5, §9.7).

claims.old: Real-time interactive operation.
claims.new: Real-time interactive operation.

claims.old: A simulation runs paced against the wall clock, with devices and a GUI attached (§10.7, §11).
claims.new: A simulation runs paced against the wall clock, with devices and a GUI attached (§10.7, §11).

claims.old: Live introspection.
claims.new: Live introspection.

claims.old: Every published signal can be inspected by path, during a run and after it (§11.2).
claims.new: Every published signal can be inspected by path, during a run and after it (§11.2).

claims.old: Compositional flexibility.
claims.new: Compositional flexibility.

claims.old: Components compose hierarchically, and a component substitutes for another behind the same declared contract (§6, §8).
claims.new: Components compose hierarchically, and a component substitutes for another behind the same declared contract (§6, §8).

claims.old: Rigor and error locality.
claims.new: Rigor and error locality.

claims.old: Structure is declared and checked at build time, so a mistake fails where it was made, with a diagnostic naming it (§8.4, §13).
claims.new: Structure is declared and checked at build time, so a mistake fails where it was made, with a diagnostic naming it (§8.4, §13).

claims.old: Components are plain Julia with no macro DSL, so debugging, tooling and comprehension work on the language's own terms (§8.1).
claims.new: Components are plain Julia with no macro DSL (domain-specific language), so debugging, tooling and comprehension work on the language's own terms (§8.1).

claims.old: Origins.
claims.new: #### Origins

claims.old: Redstone began as a replacement for `FlightCore`, the simulation core of the Flight.jl package.
claims.new: Redstone began as a replacement for `FlightCore`, the simulation core of the Flight.jl package.

claims.old: Flight.jl also holds `FlightPhysics`, its physics library, and `FlightApps`, its applications.
claims.new: Flight.jl also holds `FlightPhysics`, its physics library, and `FlightApps`, its applications.

claims.old: The early design read those two packages as its requirements.
claims.new: The early design read those two packages as its requirements.

claims.old: Every capability they demonstrated had to survive, and none of their interfaces had to.
claims.new: Every capability they demonstrated had to survive, and none of their interfaces had to.

claims.old: Older entries in the decision log reason against `FlightCore` and cite that code,
claims.new: Older entries in the decision log (`decisions.md`) reason against `FlightCore` and cite that code.

claims.old: and the case studies that tested the design against it live in `companions/flight_case_studies.md`.
claims.new: The case studies that tested the design against that code live in `companions/flight_case_studies.md`.

claims.old: Redstone itself does not depend on Flight.jl.
claims.new: Redstone itself does not depend on Flight.jl.

claims.new: This document is the normative statement of the design.

claims.new: Part II covers authoring and the build, Part III execution and the runtime periphery, and Part IV failure handling and the stopped-sim services.
